result:
My verdict is **PASS** for DG2 round 4 on candidate `sha256:29ced0ed896ab9bf…ce58` (source `e37f6ea4`). I recomputed that ID (521 files) on the working tree and in a fresh clone. F-DG2-160 is fixed and verified, every required check ran and passed, and the two new findings are both Low and non-mandatory.

During my run the orchestrator committed the domain reviewer's round-4 output, so HEAD moved from `bb4dd9c` to `3da2de1`. Those commits only add review, evidence and run files, and the candidate ID still matches. I have not opened the domain reviewer's records.

**F-DG2-160: closed and verified.**
- **Fix:** one shared "has visible content" rule (whitespace, invisible formatting characters and filler characters don't count) now backs every free-text field, the readiness checks, and the shared name and reason. The two inline reason parsers now use the shared one.
- **Round-3 repro:** passes 5/5 in two runs on a throwaway PostgreSQL. All 18 round-3 characters and 11 more are now rejected, and visible Arabic text with direction marks or emoji is still accepted as typed.
- **Performance:** the check is linear, with no ReDoS risk; 10 million invisible characters take about 0.2 s.
- **Residual bypasses:** none of the inputs I traced decides "blank" with `trim()` any more. A combining mark on its own renders a visible mark, so counting it as content is reasonable.

**No regressions in the changes since round 3.**
- **Archive and evidence-link removal reasons:** permissions are still checked first. The auditor gets 403, even with a blank reason, and an outsider gets 404. A missing If-Match gets 428 and a stale one 409. Five kinds of invisible reason each get 400 with nothing written and no audit row. A valid reason is stored trimmed with exactly one audit event.
- **OIDC change:** it only changes which claim becomes the display name for a newly provisioned user. Sign-in identity, sessions and permissions don't use it, and a new user gets no role assignments.
- **Admin issuer check:** an invisible-only issuer is now rejected as empty, at the same point in the request as before.
- **Web forms:** they block blank text inline using the same rule and send text as typed. The server still refuses the same values on its own, so the client is never the only guard. No test assertion was removed.

**Required checks: all passed.**
- **Static checks:** build, typecheck, lint, OpenAPI lint (161 operations), no-CDN and format check.
- **Unit tests:** 616/616 on Node 22 and on Node 24, and 616/616 on both again under concurrent CPU load (load average 10–14 on 4 cores). The new web blank-text tests peaked at 3.2 s against the default 5 s timeout under that load; they passed, but the margin is worth knowing.
- **Integration suite:** run twice on fresh PostgreSQL 16, 465/465 each time. Both runs covered all 19 migrations, the contract test, the blank-text tests and the AUD-403 sweep (128 + 18 tests).
- **Historical validators:** DG0 and DG1 pass.
- **Environmental residuals:** live registry, live CI and Keycloak are recorded as PASS on the offline/config side only. None was exercised live because the sandbox has no network.

**New findings.**

| ID | Severity | Mandatory | Issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| F-DG2-180 | Low | No | A set of characters that render as nothing still counts as content: variation selectors (e.g. U+FE0F), the combining grapheme joiner U+034F, Mongolian free variation selectors and Khmer inherent vowels. An Out of scope of just `"\ufe0f"` is stored (201), the B0041 pre-check reads `pass`, and G1 doesn't flag it as missing. An archive reason of three U+FE0F is accepted (200). Suggested fix: add `\p{Default_Ignorable_Code_Point}` to the shared rule in `packages/shared/src/schemas/common.ts:46`. |
| F-DG2-181 | Low | No | `apps/api/src/modules/identity/oidc.ts:167` checks the whole name claim for visible content, then stores only the first 200 characters. A name of 200 zero-width spaces followed by real text becomes an invisible display name for a newly provisioned user. It affects display only. |

I raised F-DG2-180 as a new finding rather than reopening F-DG2-160. Everything F-DG2-160 reported, and the fix it named, is done; the new gap is a different Unicode category.

All probes and runs used throwaway clones and PostgreSQL clusters, which I have removed.

Files are in `docs/delivery/reviews/DG2/round-4/`:
- `code-security-reviewer.json`
- `code-security-reviewer.findings.json`
- `code-security-reviewer.verifications.json`
- `code-security-reviewer.md`

The test evidence is under `docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG2/code-security/round-4/`.
